groups.name: At ASU
groups.blurb: Every school at ASU runs its own undergraduate research program, and almost all of them expect you to find a faculty mentor before you apply.

items.name: Fulton Undergraduate Research Initiative (FURI)
items.provider: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering, ASU
items.paid: $1,500 stipend per funded semester, plus up to $400 for research supplies. TSMC-sponsored semiconductor projects pay $2,600 plus $400.
items.commitment: One semester of research alongside your classes, ending in a poster at the Fulton Forge Student Research Expo. You can be funded for up to two semesters.
items.eligibility: Full-time Fulton Schools undergraduate in good academic standing, including ASU Online students. You need a Fulton faculty mentor who is not on sabbatical.
items.citizenship: Not stated
items.cycle: One application per semester. The page shows the Fall 2026 deadline as April 10, 2026 and late applications are never accepted, so join the notify list and watch for the next opening.
items.note: The application is the easy part. The bottleneck is landing a mentor, which means going to office hours and asking professors what they research months before the deadline. FURI also bans generative AI anywhere in the application, including your personal statement.
items.evidence: Title "FURI homepage - ASU Engineering Student Hub", HTTP 200

items.name: School of Life Sciences Undergraduate Research (SOLUR)
items.provider: School of Life Sciences, ASU
items.paid: Apprentice and Researcher levels are credit only. Scholar and Fellow levels carry funding, but the site does not publish the amount. Check the site.
items.commitment: One or two semesters in a faculty lab, plus a seminar and a poster symposium. Apprentice enrolls in BIO 189, Researcher in BIO 289.
items.eligibility: Full-time degree-seeking ASU student, 2.75 GPA for Apprentice and Researcher, 3.0 for Scholar, 3.5 for Fellow. Non-life-sciences majors qualify at the Apprentice and Researcher levels.
items.citizenship: Not stated
items.cycle: Apprentice and Researcher run on an agreement form signed by your mentor, so you can start any semester. Scholar and Fellow applications open the first week of February and close late March or early April.
items.note: Apprentice is the level built for people with no research background, but there is a catch the tiers hide: you have to already be volunteering in a lab before you can enroll. Email professors first, then apply.
items.evidence: Title "SOLUR | School of Life Sciences", HTTP 200

items.name: Economics Research Training Program
items.provider: Department of Economics, W. P. Carey School of Business, ASU
items.paid: Unpaid. Stage one is a one-credit pass/fail course.
items.commitment: Stage one is 16 weeks at about 50 minutes a week. Stage two is one to two semesters on a team of two or three students.
items.eligibility: Undergraduates in W. P. Carey or The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences who have finished ECN 221 or an equivalent statistics course with a strong grade.
items.citizenship: Not stated
items.cycle: No fixed cycle and no application form. Email the professor to ask for the next deadline, then send a one to two page CV and a one-page cover letter.
items.note: This is the one real research pathway inside W. P. Carey that starts from zero. You do not need Python or R going in, there is no interview, and students propose their own questions and can end up as co-authors. Passing stage one does not guarantee a stage two placement.
items.evidence: Title "Undergraduate Economics Program | ASU W. P. Carey", HTTP 200

items.name: Summer Research Initiative (SURI)
items.provider: Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering, ASU
items.paid: $5,000 stipend plus on-campus housing
items.commitment: Eight weeks, 30 to 40 hours a week, with the first two weeks remote. The 2026 run was May 18 to July 17.
items.eligibility: Priority goes to students between their junior and senior years and to master's students weighing a doctorate.
items.citizenship: Open to all. The page names US citizens, permanent residents, ASU-sponsored F-1 and J-1 students, and international applicants.
items.cycle: Applications close in the winter for a May start. The page currently reads "Applications for SURI 2026 are closed now", so watch it over winter break.
items.note: Rare among funded summer research programs because it does not shut out international students. If you are on an F-1 visa and have been turned away from REUs, start here.
items.evidence: Title "Summer Research Initiative (SURI) - ASU Engineering Student Hub", HTTP 200

items.name: Online Undergraduate Research Scholars (OURS)
items.provider: The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, ASU
items.paid: No stipend. Some projects are credit-bearing courses you pay tuition for. A separate OURS scholarship exists with preference for high financial need.
items.commitment: 5 to 20 hours a week. The program advises blocking out long stretches rather than an hour here and there.
items.eligibility: ASU Online students in a College of Liberal Arts and Sciences degree. On-campus students are not eligible.
items.citizenship: Not stated
items.cycle: Two cycles a year. The Fall 2026 application posted May 22 and closed July 15, 2026.
items.note: Group-based, so you are not cold-emailing a professor to get in. Since 2022 more than half of participants have been Pell eligible and 38 percent underrepresented minorities, which tells you who actually gets picked.
items.evidence: Title "Online students | OURS Program", HTTP 200

items.name: Research Apprenticeship Program
items.provider: School of Human Evolution and Social Change, ASU
items.paid: Unpaid. Credit through ASB 499 or ASB 484, 1 to 3 credits, and whether you get credit is up to the lead faculty member.
items.commitment: Set by a research contract based on the hours you commit each week. Projects are sorted into entry, mid and upper level.
items.eligibility: All majors are encouraged to apply, with preference to School of Human Evolution and Social Change students. Online students can join projects that allow remote work.
items.citizenship: Not stated
items.cycle: One deadline per semester. The Fall 2026 deadline was June 24, 2026 at 5 p.m. MST.
items.note: One of the few ASU programs where you apply to a posted project instead of finding your own mentor, and where explicit entry-level slots exist. Apply to several projects, each as a separate submission.
items.evidence: Title "Research Apprenticeship Program | School of Human Evolution and Social Change", HTTP 200

items.name: Sustainability Undergraduate Research Experience (SURE)
items.provider: School of Sustainability, ASU
items.paid: Not stated. Check the site.
items.commitment: Research in the spring C session. You can enroll in three credits of independent research but it is not required.
items.eligibility: On-campus and online undergraduates. No major, class standing or GPA requirement stated.
items.citizenship: Not stated
items.cycle: Applications open in the fall and are due mid-October. Faculty pick students in November for a spring start.
items.note: The mid-October deadline is the nearest one on this whole list. The program says taking SOS 246 in fall A session improves your odds, which is really a hint that they want people who already know what a research question is.
items.evidence: Title "SURE Program - School of Sustainability", HTTP 200

items.name: UResearch, the ASU research opportunity directory
items.provider: Office of the University Provost, ASU
items.paid: Varies by program. The directory itself pays nothing.
items.commitment: Varies
items.eligibility: Any ASU undergraduate
items.citizenship: Varies by program
items.cycle: Always open
items.note: This is the master list. It links more than 40 unit-level research programs, including ones nobody talks about in W. P. Carey, plus the psychology, math, molecular sciences and earth and space programs. Read it once and pick three to email.
items.evidence: Title "UResearch | University Provost | ASU", HTTP 200

items.name: Barrett honors research and thesis pathway
items.provider: Barrett, The Honors College, ASU
items.paid: Not stated. Check the site.
items.commitment: Honors credit attached to a research experience, building toward the honors thesis or creative project.
items.eligibility: Barrett students. Barrett says it works with every school at ASU to match students with research as early as their first year.
items.citizenship: Not stated
items.cycle: Rolling. The thesis itself is usually started in junior year with a defense in senior year.
items.note: The thesis is the reason to be in Barrett if you want research, because it forces you into a committee with faculty who then write your recommendation letters. The page names a coordinator, which is a faster route than the web form.
items.evidence: Title "Research | Barrett, The Honors College | ASU", HTTP 200

items.name: ASU student employment and Handshake research postings
items.provider: Arizona State University
items.paid: Hourly, varies by posting
items.commitment: Usually 10 to 20 hours a week during the semester
items.eligibility: Enrolled ASU students. Work-study eligibility widens what you can apply to.
items.citizenship: International students on F-1 can hold on-campus jobs. Check the posting.
items.cycle: Rolling. Most lab hiring happens in the two weeks before a semester starts.
items.note: Paid undergraduate research assistant jobs are posted here and on Handshake as ordinary student jobs, not as research programs. Search the word "research assistant" rather than browsing categories, and check weekly, because these fill in days.
items.evidence: Title "Student Employment at Arizona State University", HTTP 200

groups.name: Built for first-generation and underrepresented students
groups.blurb: These exist because the usual route into research runs through people you already know, and most of our members do not have that.

items.name: WAESO, the Western Alliance to Expand Student Opportunities (LSAMP)
items.provider: National Science Foundation, alliance headquartered at ASU
items.paid: Research stipends and conference travel are part of the model, but no amount is published anywhere we could verify. Check with your advisor.
items.commitment: Mentored research with a STEM faculty member during the academic year, plus peer study groups.
items.eligibility: Undergraduates from groups underrepresented in STEM at the 13 alliance institutions across Arizona, Utah and Colorado. ASU is the lead institution.
items.citizenship: Not stated
items.cycle: Runs on the academic year. Ask early in the fall.
items.note: ASU runs this alliance but its student-facing site at waeso.asu.edu no longer resolves in DNS, so there is nowhere online to apply. Go through a Fulton or College STEM advisor and ask who administers LSAMP now. The link here is the national NSF program page.
items.evidence: Title "Louis Stokes Alliances for Minority Participation (LSAMP) | NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation", HTTP 200. waeso.asu.edu fails to resolve.

items.name: HACU National Internship Program (HNIP)
items.provider: Hispanic Association of Colleges and Universities
items.paid: $18.50 an hour for undergraduates in 2026, $20.25 for graduate students
items.commitment: Ten weeks in summer 2026, nine weeks in summer 2027, fifteen weeks for fall and spring sessions
items.eligibility: Any race or ethnicity, all majors, minimum 2.0 GPA preferred, must have completed your first year.
items.citizenship: Most federal placements require US citizenship, but the program explicitly encourages permanent residents, DACA students and anyone legally authorized to work in the US to apply.
items.cycle: Four sessions a year. Spring 2027 priority deadline is November 20, 2026. Summer 2027 opens October 1, 2026 with a March 6, 2027 priority deadline.
items.note: The only paid national program on this list that names DACA students in writing. Placements are federal agencies, and several of them are research shops, so filter the open positions by agency rather than by job title.
items.evidence: Title "HNIP Overview", HTTP 200

items.name: Leadership Alliance Summer Research Early Identification Program (SR-EIP)
items.provider: The Leadership Alliance, a consortium of research universities
items.paid: Fully paid. Stipend plus travel and housing, paid by the host institution. The amount varies by site.
items.commitment: Eight to ten weeks in the summer
items.eligibility: Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors with a 3.0 GPA or better who intend to pursue a PhD or MD-PhD. Not for people heading to law, business, clinical medicine or allied health.
items.citizenship: US citizen, non-citizen national, or permanent resident with an I-551. F-1 visa holders, asylum seekers and refugees are not eligible.
items.cycle: Opens November 1 and closes in early February. The 2026 cycle opened November 1, 2025 and closed February 3, 2026.
items.note: One application reaches every member university, which is why it is worth the effort. Prior research is preferred at some sites and not required at others, so read each site's page instead of assuming you are underqualified.
items.evidence: Title "Summer Research Early Identification Program | The Leadership Alliance", HTTP 200

items.name: Pathways to Science
items.provider: Institute for Broadening Participation
items.paid: Varies by listing
items.commitment: Varies
items.eligibility: Undergraduates, with a filter for programs aimed at underrepresented students
items.citizenship: Varies by listing, and the database lets you filter for programs open to non-citizens
items.cycle: Always open. Most summer listings post between October and January.
items.note: Use this instead of the NSF REU list when citizenship is a problem, because you can filter for programs that accept non-citizens. That filter does not exist on the NSF site.
items.evidence: Title "Pathways To Science | Increasing Diversity in STEM", HTTP 200

groups.name: National summer programs
groups.blurb: Paid ten-week summers at labs and universities across the country, almost all of which decide in the winter for the following June.

items.name: NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU)
items.provider: National Science Foundation, hosted at universities and labs nationwide
items.paid: Paid. Stipend, housing and travel are set by each individual site, so amounts vary.
items.commitment: Usually ten weeks full time in the summer
items.eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled in a degree program, including community college students. Each site sets its own class-standing rules.
items.citizenship: US citizen, national, or permanent resident. This is an NSF-wide rule, not a site preference, and it excludes international and undocumented students from nearly every REU.
items.cycle: Sites post in the fall. Most deadlines land between January and early March for a June start.
items.note: Apply to eight or ten sites, not two. Many now take applications through NSF's ETAP portal at etap.nsf.gov, which lets one profile feed several applications. Sites explicitly want students whose own campus has no research program, which cuts against ASU applicants at ASU-hosted REUs.
items.evidence: Title "NSF Research Experiences for Undergraduates | NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation", HTTP 200

items.name: Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internships (SULI)
items.provider: US Department of Energy, Office of Science, at the national laboratories
items.paid: $650 a week, plus one round-trip travel reimbursement if you live more than 50 miles away and a housing allowance where the lab does not provide housing
items.commitment: Ten consecutive weeks in summer, or sixteen weeks for a semester term
items.eligibility: Full-time undergraduate, at least 18, 3.0 cumulative GPA, at least one completed semester, at least 6 STEM credit hours and 12 total credit hours. AP credit does not count.
items.citizenship: US citizen or lawful permanent resident at the time of application, with proof required before you start.
items.cycle: Three terms a year. Spring 2027 applications are due September 30, 2026 at 5 p.m. ET. The summer term deadline is usually in January.
items.note: The semester terms are far less competitive than summer and nobody applies to them. You can do SULI twice and apply up to four times, so a rejection is not the end. Permanent residents should contact the lab early because site access clearance takes time.
items.evidence: Title "Science Undergraduate Laboratory... | U.S. DOE Office of Science (SC)", HTTP 200

items.name: SMART Scholarship for Service
items.provider: US Department of Defense, listed by ASU's Office of National Scholarships Advisement
items.paid: $25,000 to $38,000 a year in stipend depending on degree level, plus full tuition and paid summer internships at a DoD lab
items.commitment: One year of employment at a DoD facility for every year of funding. Awards run one to five years.
items.eligibility: 18 or older, 3.0 cumulative GPA, enrolled at an accredited US college in a listed STEM discipline, and willing to take post-graduate DoD employment.
items.citizenship: US citizen at the time of application. No exceptions.
items.cycle: Deadline in December each year
items.note: This is a job offer wearing a scholarship's clothes, and the service commitment is real. ASU's ONSA office advises on the application and will read your essays, which is worth more than the official site. You also have to be able to hold a security clearance.
items.evidence: Title "SMART Scholarship for Service Program | Office of National Scholarships Advisement | ASU", HTTP 200

items.name: Amgen Scholars
items.provider: Amgen Foundation, hosted at 14 universities including Caltech, Columbia, Harvard, Howard, Stanford, UC Berkeley, UCLA and Yale
items.paid: Housing, food and travel covered, with details set by each host. Symposium travel is fully funded.
items.commitment: Eight to ten weeks in the summer, typically June through August
items.eligibility: Sophomores, juniors and non-graduating seniors at accredited four-year US institutions with a 3.2 GPA or above who are interested in a PhD or MD-PhD.
items.citizenship: US citizens and permanent residents only. International students are not eligible.
items.cycle: All hosts share an early February deadline, February 1 in the 2026 cycle. Decisions by the end of March.
items.note: About 140 slots nationally, and you apply to each host separately, so treat it as 14 applications. The program says outright it takes students with no prior lab experience, which is unusual at this level of prestige.
items.evidence: Title "United States - Amgen Scholars", HTTP 200

items.name: NIH Summer Internship Program (SIP)
items.provider: National Institutes of Health, Intramural Research Program, Bethesda MD and other campuses
items.paid: Paid. Stipends are set annually by education level and are not published on the program page. Check the site.
items.commitment: Full time for the summer. The program states plainly that you cannot take summer classes or hold other obligations during work hours.
items.eligibility: Enrolled at least half time in an accredited community college, college, university or graduate program, and 18 by September 30 of the program year.
items.citizenship: US citizen or permanent resident. Permanent residents must be attending a US institution.
items.cycle: The Summer 2027 application opens mid-November 2026 and closes mid-February 2027. Reference letters get an extra week.
items.note: NIH does not provide housing and Bethesda is expensive, so budget for that before you accept. Community college students are eligible, which almost no other program on this list allows. Contacting principal investigators directly before you apply is how most people actually get matched.
items.evidence: Title "Summer Internship Program (SIP) | Office of Intramural Training & Education at the National Institutes of Health", loaded 200 in a browser. Plain curl returns 403 from Cloudflare.

groups.name: Business and economics research
groups.blurb: The hardest bucket to fill, because business schools run almost no undergraduate research, so the real openings are at the Federal Reserve and the think tanks.

items.name: Sophomore Career Exploration Program
items.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
items.paid: Paid. Amount not published. Check the site.
items.commitment: Ten weeks starting in early June, in one business area
items.eligibility: Undergraduate sophomores. For the summer 2027 program, students expecting to graduate in December 2027 or spring 2028.
items.citizenship: Not stated on the program page
items.cycle: Application window September 1 to September 28, 2026 for a June 2027 start.
items.note: The deadline is two weeks from now and it is the earliest serious research-adjacent door open to a sophomore anywhere on this list. You need a resume and a transcript. Letters of recommendation are not read, so do not chase them.
items.evidence: Title "Sophomore Career Exploration Program - FEDERAL RESERVE BANK of NEW YORK", HTTP 200

items.name: Undergraduate Summer Analyst Program
items.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
items.paid: Paid. Amount not published. Check the site.
items.commitment: Ten weeks starting in early June, project-based work in one business area with an assigned mentor
items.eligibility: Undergraduate juniors. For the summer 2027 program, students expecting to graduate in December 2026 or spring 2027.
items.citizenship: Not stated on the program page
items.cycle: Application window September 1 to October 5, 2026 for a June 2027 start.
items.note: The New York Fed says full-time Research Analysts are usually first met through these internships, so this is the audition for the two-year research job. Twenty days left as of mid-September.
items.evidence: Title "Undergraduate Summer Analyst Program - FEDERAL RESERVE BANK of NEW YORK", HTTP 200

items.name: Research Analyst Program
items.provider: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Research and Statistics Group
items.paid: Full-time salaried position with a 401(k) match, commutation assistance and tuition reimbursement
items.commitment: Two years full time, starting the summer after you graduate
items.eligibility: Graduating college seniors with a background in economics, mathematics or statistics and experience in R, Stata, Matlab, Python or similar. Roughly twenty hired a year.
items.citizenship: Not stated on the program page
items.cycle: Applications for a summer 2027 start ran August 24 to September 14. That window closed yesterday, so the next one opens in late August 2027.
items.note: This is the standard route into a top economics PhD and many RAs co-author published papers. The window is three weeks long and closes before most people start thinking about it, which is the whole reason to know the date now. Resume and transcript only, and letters of recommendation are explicitly not considered.
items.evidence: Title "Research Analysts - FEDERAL RESERVE BANK of NEW YORK", HTTP 200

items.name: Federal Reserve Board summer internships
items.provider: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Washington DC
items.paid: Paid, with salary set by years of higher education completed. Exact rates are not published. Check the site.
items.commitment: Ten to twelve weeks starting late May or early June
items.eligibility: Currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate student returning to study after the internship. Selection weighs coursework, recommendations and sometimes GPA.
items.citizenship: US citizens only. The Board states this outright.
items.cycle: Most postings go up in September for the following summer. Virtual interviews run through the fall and offers are finalized by December.
items.note: Offers are done by December, so a spring application is not late, it is pointless. Each posting lists its own requirements, so read them individually rather than assuming one generic application exists.
items.evidence: Title "The Fed - Internships", HTTP 200

items.name: Fed Econ Jobs
items.provider: Federal Reserve System, all 12 district banks plus the Board
items.paid: Varies by location
items.commitment: Research assistant roles are generally two-year full-time positions after graduation
items.eligibility: Varies by district. Preferred coursework and technical skills are listed per location.
items.citizenship: Varies by district
items.cycle: Most hiring happens in the fall. Atlanta runs September 1 to October 3, Boston August 21 to September 30, Philadelphia September through March, Minneapolis late winter or early spring.
items.note: Everyone applies to New York and nobody applies to Kansas City or Cleveland, and the work is the same. Thirteen locations means thirteen shots, and the windows are staggered enough that missing one does not end your year.
items.evidence: Title "FedEconJobs Home | Fed Econ Jobs", HTTP 200

items.name: AEA Summer Training and Scholarship Program
items.provider: American Economic Association, hosted at American University
items.paid: $3,250 stipend on completion for US citizens, permanent residents and DACA students whose visa allows the payment. The package also covers tuition, fees, living expenses, transportation, books and excursions.
items.commitment: Two-month intensive residential program, June 1 to July 24 in the 2026 run, earning up to 12 college credits
items.eligibility: Undergraduates without a PhD in economics. Ideally a 3.0 GPA in relevant courses. You need micro, macro and Calculus 1 at a minimum because the program is heavily mathematical.
items.citizenship: Open to all. International students may apply and be admitted, but receive no stipend or scholarship and are responsible for costs estimated at just over $25,000. DACA students do receive the $3,250.
items.cycle: Applications close January 31. The 2026 portal closed February 1, 2026 and the page is still showing that past cycle.
items.note: Running since 1974 and the single best-known feeder into economics PhD programs for underrepresented students. It is training, not a research placement, so it fixes the math gap that keeps W. P. Carey students out of RA jobs. Anyone can apply regardless of ethnicity.
items.evidence: Title "AEA Summer Training and Scholarship Program", HTTP 200

items.name: Economics research assistantships and internships list
items.provider: Department of Economics, W. P. Carey School of Business, ASU
items.paid: Varies by employer
items.commitment: Most are one to two year full-time positions after you graduate
items.eligibility: Aimed at students heading for a PhD or a research career. Brookings and AEI also take current upperclassmen for internships.
items.citizenship: Varies by employer
items.cycle: Varies. Most predoc and RA postings appear between August and October.
items.note: ASU's own curated list, pointing at the Fed, the IMF, Stanford GSB, Columbia, NBER, Brookings, AEI, Urban, Heritage, RAND, the Department of Labor and USDA Economic Research Service. Read it as a senior-year list, not a sophomore one, because most entries require a completed bachelor's.
items.evidence: Title "About Economics Assistantships and Internships | ASU", HTTP 200

items.name: PREDOC opportunities board
items.provider: Pathways to Research and Doctoral Careers (PREDOC)
items.paid: Paid full-time positions. Amounts are set per posting.
items.commitment: One to two years full time
items.eligibility: Every position requires a bachelor's degree by the start date, so this is for graduating seniors.
items.citizenship: Varies by posting
items.cycle: Postings concentrate in August through October for the following summer. Stanford GSB closed October 16, 2026 and Opportunity Insights October 1, 2026 in the current cycle. Many are rolling.
items.note: This is where predoc jobs at Harvard Business School, MIT Blueprint Labs, Yale and Opportunity Insights get posted, and it is not a place for current undergraduates to find summer work. Bookmark it in your junior year and apply the September you graduate.
items.evidence: Title "Opportunities | Pathways to Research and Doctoral Careers", HTTP 200

notes_for_integration: ASU does NOT host a McNair Scholars program. ASU's TRIO page (access.asu.edu/trio, HTTP 200) lists nine federal TRIO programs, four pre-college and five college programs, and the college ones are Student Support Services, not McNair. The only McNair program in Arizona is at the University of Arizona and it serves UA students only. ASU does waive graduate application fees for McNair scholars from other institutions, which is the only ASU connection. Left out as an item because an ASU undergraduate cannot apply to it. Same reasoning for NIH MARC and U-RISE: no ASU-hosted site was found, and the Arizona MARC program is at the University of Arizona. WAESO/LSAMP is a real problem. ASU is the lead institution of the alliance and NSF renewed the grant, but the student-facing site at waeso.asu.edu does not resolve in DNS at all (confirmed against 8.8.8.8), and waeso.org times out on curl. There is currently no verifiable online application path, so the item points at the national NSF page and tells students to ask an advisor. Somebody at the chapter should call the Fulton Schools and find out who administers LSAMP now before this ships. ASU's School of Molecular Sciences runs an NSF REU (sms.asu.edu/reu, HTTP 200) with a $6,000 stipend, free housing and no prior experience required, and it was deliberately left out: eligibility is restricted to students at US colleges WITHOUT graduate chemistry programs, which excludes ASU students from ASU's own REU. The page is also still showing the 2024 cycle. Same trap applies broadly, REU sites prefer students whose home campus has no research infrastructure, so ASU students should target REUs elsewhere. ASU BIOS also runs an REU (bios.asu.edu/education/nsf-reu, HTTP 200) but it is a fall-only ocean sciences program in Bermuda with 2027 details not yet posted, and it was left out as too narrow. Stipend figures we could NOT confirm on a live page and therefore wrote as 'Check the site': SOLUR Scholar and Fellow funding, NY Fed sophomore and junior internship pay, Federal Reserve Board intern salary, NIH SIP stipend, SURE pay. The SMART figure of $25,000 to $38,000 comes from ASU's own ONSA page, not the SMART site, which is a JavaScript shell that returns nothing useful to curl and refuses a headless browser. Several pages are showing past cycles as of 2026-09-15 and the items say so: FURI (Fall 2026 deadline of April 10, 2026 shown as closed), SURI (2026 closed), Amgen Scholars (February 1, 2026), Leadership Alliance (February 3, 2026), AEA Summer Program (portal closed February 1, 2026), SMS REU (2024). The near-term deadlines worth putting in front of members right now are NY Fed sophomore on September 28, SULI Spring 2027 on September 30, NY Fed junior on October 5, SURE in mid-October and HNIP Spring 2027 on November 20. The NY Fed Research Analyst window closed on September 14, one day before this was compiled. Two items are internships rather than research strictly speaking, HNIP and the Federal Reserve Board internships, and both are included because the placements are research shops and because they are among the very few paid options that do not require a faculty sponsor you have to find yourself.
